targets.title: Improving problem solving with subgoal labels in procedural instructions and worked examples
targets.evidence_quote:
In line with these predictions, Margulieux and Catrambone (2016) found that subgoal
labels improved learning for a programming task most if they were placed in the exposi-
tory text and worked examples.

It was hypothesized that the pattern of results in the new domains would replicate those
found in the programming domain. That is, subgoal labeled expository texts would interact
with subgoal labeled worked examples to produce the best problem solving performance.
targets.outcome_quote:
For both procedures that were studied, subgoal labeled worked examples had a consistent
effect: improved problem solving performance. These results align with the original Mar-
gulieux and Catrambone (2016) study and other previous research (e.g., Catrambone 1998;
Margulieux et al. 2016), suggesting that subgoal labels reliably help students learn from
worked examples more effectively. For subgoal labeled expository text, however, the effect
differed in both domains, and neither matched the pattern of results found in programming.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly report agreement for worked examples and disagreement for expository text in both new domains. The discussion does not give an overall replication verdict that supersedes these comparisons.
